# Lindela Lite

> Open-source climate-conflict and flood-impact toolkit. Ingests public data,
> normalizes it into simple schemas, computes transparent baseline risk scores,
> and serves them over an HTTP API with a no-build frontend.

This file is the map an agent needs to work in this repository without reading
all 28,000 lines. It is a map, not a summary — where a claim here matters, the
source file is the authority.

- Package: `@lindela/lite`, private, MIT, Node >= 20, ESM throughout.
- Runtime dependencies: `pg` and nothing else. `npm test` needs no database.
- Single process, single port (`LINDELA_LITE_PORT` or 4177), single Postgres
  table (`lite_records`) or a single JSON file.

## Verify before you claim

```bash
npm test              # node --test test/*.test.js
npm run validate      # model-basis status, capability guard, i18n
                      # completeness, documentation links, and the OpenAPI
                      # document against the route table
npm run test:coverage # thresholds: lines 75, branches 60, functions 75
```

`validate` used to check that a hand-maintained endpoint list in
`scripts/validate.mjs` appeared in `docs/openapi.yaml`. That tested the list, not
the server: adding a route and forgetting the list passed, which is how nine live
routes went undocumented. `scripts/check-openapi.mjs` now reads the routes out of
`src/server.js` and requires the two to agree in both directions — see *The API
document is checked, not trusted* below.

It also used not to check documentation links, with the same consequence: the ADR
table in `docs/architecture/decisions/README.md` listed twelve records while six
of the files did not exist, and every check passed.
`scripts/check-doc-links.mjs` resolves every relative markdown link under
`README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `llms.txt` and `docs/**/*.md`, stripping fenced and
inline code first so a bracket in a CSV example is not read as a link. A dangling
link fails *silently* otherwise — the document renders, reads well, and lies.

`npm test` and `npm run validate` must both exit 0. Never gate a check on a
pipe (`npm test | tail -5`) — `tail` masks the exit code and truncates the
pass/fail summary, which is the last line. Redirect to a file and read it.

## The rule that governs the whole codebase

**Flood probability here is empirical co-occurrence, not hydrology.** It is not
a return period, not a recurrence interval, not an annual exceedance
probability. Any of that vocabulary appearing in the tree fails the build via
`scripts/check-no-flood-probability.mjs`, which scans `src/`, `public/`,
`scripts/`, `test/`, and `docs/`. The one permitted exception is
`docs/flood-probability-model-basis.md`.

This extends into the payload contract:

- Risk "percentiles" are **sensitivity bands**. They were renamed so they would
  stop reading as quantiles.
- `false_alert: null` means *not determined*, not zero.
- A missing forecast is not a 0% chance of rain.
- `0` and `null` are different. A coordinate at 0° is a coordinate. Use
  `Number.isFinite(Number(x))`, never truthiness, on nullable numerics.

When you add a numeric output, ask what qualification the docs carry and whether
it reaches the caller. Half of them historically did not.

## Layout

| Path | What lives there |
|---|---|
| `src/server.js` | The router. ~2,700 lines, every `/api/v1/*` route. |
| `src/store.js` | `JsonStore` + the `COLLECTIONS` list every store keys off. |
| `src/postgres-store.js` | `PostgresStore`. Same contract, different backend. |
| `src/schema.js` | Normalized record shapes and `emptyStore()`. |
| `src/ingestion.js` | `runIngestion`, `OUTPUT_COLLECTIONS`, source policies. |
| `src/connectors/` | 17 connectors; `spec.js` is the SDK (`defineConnector`). |
| `public/shared/charts.js` | Five chart primitives + `sparkline`. **Pure**: every function returns strings, no DOM, so `test/charts.test.js` asserts on what was drawn without a browser. Rules: an absent value is never a zero, every chart ships an `aria-hidden` SVG plus a table sibling, one shared data-derived extent, colour only from tokens. |
| `src/upload.js` | `POST /api/v1/upload`. Bulk CSV import: per-collection column contract, row-level validation report, `dry_run`. A batch with any rejected row writes nothing — see `docs/api.md` § Bulk Upload. |
| `src/analytics/` | Flood probability, impact, downscaling, ensemble. |
| `public/` | Eight PWA surfaces. No framework, no build step, no bundler. |
| `test/` | `node:test`. `store-conformance.test.js` runs one contract against every backend. |
| `docs/` | Architecture, OpenAPI, improvements audit, model basis. |
| `docs/improvements/` | Four documents: `enhancements.md` (ENH-01..30, can it be trusted), `defects.md` (~55 defects + a remediation index), `roadmap-extension.md` (items 1–20, does what shipped actually work), `sources-and-decisions-roadmap.md` (31 items, what does it not know yet). They carry a dedup ledger against each other — do not add an item to one that another already owns. |

## Three lists that must agree

`COLLECTIONS` (store), `OUTPUT_COLLECTIONS` (ingestion), `emptyStore()`
(schema). When they drift, records vanish with no error anywhere: the producer
writes them, the consumer never asks for them, and every number still looks
plausible.

The same class of bug has appeared four times in this repository. Guard it with
behaviour — assert that a stub connector's records come back out of the store —
never by grepping source text for a collection name. Two guards that did exactly
that passed with the bug fully present.

## An import is a claim about a dependency

`test/unused-imports.test.js` fails the build when a named import in `src/` or
`scripts/` is never mentioned again in its own file. Ten were, at last count,
six of them in `server.js`.

An import is the only place a reader learns that one module depends on another,
so a file full of them makes its own dependency graph wrong in the reader's
head. There is no linter here, so the test is the linter. It also asserts that it
read a real tree before reporting anything clean — a scanner that matched nothing
would produce the same result as a scanner that found nothing wrong, and the
distinction is invisible from the outside.

## Strings live in `en.json`, and the gate measures them

`scripts/check-i18n.mjs`, run by `npm run validate`, enforces two rules over
every surface: a `data-i18n` key in the DOM must exist in `en.json`, and a
locale a page offers must be able to render every string that page shows. A
surface with no keys at all is reported by name rather than counted as passing.

The gate holds an absolute floor on each locale's translated count, never a
percentage. A percentage floor moves every time a key is added, which would turn
the check into an argument with the catalogue instead of a measurement of it; and
it would have to be met by guessing at new strings rather than by translating
them. Adding 217 keys to `en.json` dropped `sw` from 92% to 48% coverage and
changed no `sw` string, which is the right shape for that number to move.

## Storage backends

Four modes via `LINDELA_LITE_DB_MODE`: `auto`, `postgres`, `pg0`, `json`.
`postgres` and `pg0` are the same `PostgresStore`; `auto` prefers Postgres if
`DATABASE_URL` is set, then pg0, then JSON.

The two backends must agree. `JsonStore.replaceAnalytics` stores six derived
collections; `PostgresStore`'s once took four, so the impact figures were
computed and silently dropped on Postgres alone. `test/store-conformance.test.js`
is what makes that class of divergence impossible to reintroduce — it needs
`LINDELA_LITE_TEST_DATABASE_URL` set to exercise the Postgres half.

## Reporting a number

The repository has one recurring shape of bug, and it is not a typo: a figure
is computed from something other than what its name says, and it looks
plausible. Instances fixed so far, each with a test that fails without the fix:

- `response_rate_pct` divided messages by dispatches and reported 200%. It now
  counts distinct people, and is `null` — not `0` — when the figure is not
  computable.
- Dispatch precision divided by every dispatch while subtracting false positives
  from alerts never dispatched.
- `false_alert_rate` was computed over a 30-row window and reported as the
  district's rate.
- An unfitted model rendered "0% flood-month base rate"; an absent severity
  passed every severity filter.

So: **an absent value is not a zero, and an unevaluated thing is not a false
one.** Prefer `null` with a note over a number that would have to be explained.
`src/equity.js`, `src/rapidpro.js` and `src/parametric.js` all carry this
convention in their field comments.

## The API substrate

Four things every list route and every mutation now has. See `src/utils.js`.

- **List routes return a total, not just a page.** `{ data, returned, limit,
  total, has_more, next_cursor }`. `total` counts everything that matched the
  filters; `data` is one page. Without it a caller cannot tell an empty
  collection from a truncated one. Page with `?cursor=<next_cursor>&limit=N`.
  An unknown cursor is a 400 — silently restarting from the top looks like
  progress and is not.
- **200s carry an `ETag`** and honour `If-None-Match` with a bodyless 304. This
  is why `jsonResponse` reads `res.req`: Node populates it, so the request
  reaches the response without being threaded through thirty-odd call sites.
- **`Idempotency-Key` on mutating requests.** A repeat replays the original
  response. The key is scoped by caller, method and path before lookup, and a
  key reused with a different body is a 409. In-process, 24h, capped at 1000
  entries — a bounded guarantee, reported by `/api/v1/ready`, never implied.
- **`/api/v1/health` is liveness; `/api/v1/ready` is readiness.** The store is a
  separate dependency. `/ready` probes it, times out, and returns 503 with the
  error, so a load balancer can route around an instance that cannot serve.

## The API document is checked, not trusted

`scripts/check-openapi.mjs` parses `src/server.js` — literal
`url.pathname === '...'` conditions and the eleven `match*Route` dispatchers —
and fails if `docs/openapi.yaml` and the served routes disagree in either
direction. Adding a route without documenting it fails; deleting one without
undocumenting it fails.

Two things about the checker worth knowing before you touch it. First, it
compares **paths, not method/path pairs**: a sub-handler serving GET on a list
and POST on a detail is modelled as serving both on both, because the fine
method gating is not worth parsing and a wrong method is a documentation nicety
while a wrong path is a broken client. Second, it prints what it parsed and
what it could not, so the claim "the document matches the server" is always
backed by a number. A checker that silently stops checking is worse than none.

Three traps in parsing a path-matching regex, all of which produce plausible
wrong answers rather than errors:

- every separator is **escaped** (`/^\/api\/v1\/webhooks$/`), so a scanner
  that treats `\` as opaque finds no separator at all;
- an **unescaped** `/` is not a separator — `([^/]+)` contains one inside a
  character class;
- a group is **not always a parameter**: `(copy)` is one segment and
  `(approve|reject)` is two, and reading either as a parameter invents
  `/api/v1/x/{id}/{id}` and hides the routes that exist.

## The frontend derives its precache, it does not list it

`public/sw.js` exports `shellGraph(load, origin)`, a breadth-first closure over
`<link href>`, `<script src>`, `@import` and `from '…'`, starting from eight
`ENTRY_PATHS` plus four `BOOTSTRAP_ASSETS`. Cross-origin and `/api/` references
are dropped. The point is not the mechanism: the point is that a hand-kept list
of an import graph is wrong the moment anyone adds an import, and that the list
was wrong three times in a row — five paths, then eight shared modules, then the
entry points — each repair a snapshot and each snapshot an omission. A missing
ES module is a hard module-resolution error, not a degraded load, so the console
failed to boot offline entirely.

`shellGraph` takes its loader as an argument precisely so the closure can be
tested without a browser: `test/web-chw-offline.test.js` runs it against the real
`public/` tree on disk. If you add an import, that test is what stops the worker
from going stale — do not reintroduce a constant.

**The frontend gates mostly need a browser and mostly have not been run.** The
family is `check:a11y`, `check:responsive`, `check:dashboard`. They require Chrome
on `:9222` and a server on `:4177`, and CI runs none of them. A fix in those files
is a claim until someone runs the gate; `docs/improvements/defects.md` marks
WEB-10 exactly that way.

## CI

`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, jobs `test`, `coverage`, `audit`, `sbom`,
`live-sources`, `dashboard`, and `provenance` (tag pushes only, gated on the
first four).

**There is no Postgres in CI.** No job sets `LINDELA_LITE_TEST_DATABASE_URL`, so
`test/store-conformance.test.js` runs its Postgres half as a silent skip and
`src/postgres-store.js` sits near 0% function coverage in the coverage gate —
on the backend every production deployment selects. Treat that as a known gap,
not as a passing test.

## Conventions

- Node package; the Python conventions in the surrounding `CLAUDE.md` do not apply.
- Tests use `node:test`. No mocking — real objects, real local HTTP server.
- Records are keyed on `id`, minted by `stableId(prefix, parts)`.
- Every connector declares a `rateLimit` in its policy. Whether it is *enforced*
  is a separate question — check, do not assume.
